description: Participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 and looking forward to building a project using NASA's data and resources.
summary: Abandoned but Not Forgotten is a story-driven website that introduces school-age space fans to the hardware NASA has left on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space. Eleven machines each get a card with a first-person line in the machine's own voice, what it did, its status today, and the science it made possible, from Surveyor 3 and the Apollo Lunar Module to Viking, Spirit, Opportunity, Ingenuity, Pioneer 10 and Voyager 1. An interactive timeline, Moon/Mars/Deep space filters, a short quiz and an animated starfield make the history engaging. Every card links to its NASA source. It matters because most young people only hear about active missions, while these silent machines hold remarkable stories and discoveries.
details: The project is a single-page website built with plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with no frameworks, and hosted on GitHub Pages. All content sits in one data list that generates the timeline and cards. Each card gives a first-person opening line, what the machine did, its current status, what scientists learned from it, and a link to its NASA page. Visitors can click the timeline to jump to a story, filter by Moon, Mars or deep space, and take a six-question quiz. A canvas-drawn animated sky (twinkling stars, a ringed planet, shooting stars and click sparkles) sets the mood and turns itself off for people who prefer reduced motion. The tone is written for ages roughly 10 to 14. We focused on accuracy by using NASA mission pages and the NSSDCA archive as sources and checking every fact against them.
